question: Does a coalesced asyncThrottle caller await the execution that will persist its latest arguments?

sources.name: TanStack Query asyncThrottle source
sources.claim: A call made while a later execution is already scheduled updates the selected arguments but can return before those arguments execute.

sources.name: Accepted asyncThrottle candidate
sources.claim: One pending execution generation owns one shared completion promise, while calls after execution begins form a later generation.

sources.name: Exact focused execution carrier
sources.claim: Exact-base verification, frozen install, formatting, existing and new tests, ESLint, and current TypeScript passed against the accepted candidate.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The original coalesced caller settles while only the active execution has run.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The original promise acknowledges scheduling rather than completion of the selected snapshot.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Candidate callers coalesced into one pending generation receive the same promise and settle after the latest arguments execute.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The selected repair binds acknowledgement to the execution generation that owns those arguments.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Calls after a generation starts execution form one distinct later generation and coalesce only with each other.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The repair preserves separate ownership across active and pending executions.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Existing long-execution throttle tests and all focused repository gates pass at the accepted head.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The repaired scheduler preserves established immediate-call and interval behavior in the tested package surface.

stop_condition: Stop after exact-head target execution, complete three-file diff review, and execution-carrier retirement.
